current_example.problem:
Consider two sets of $30$ paired observations $x_{1}, x_2, \ldots, x_{30},$ and $y_{1}, y_2, \ldots, y_{30}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{x}_{i}=315, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{y}_{i}=278, \\  & {\sum }_{i=1}^{30}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}=2\,964.\end{aligned}
$$

Determine $S_{xy}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations $x_{1}, x_2, \ldots, x_{n}$ and $y_{1}, y_2, \ldots, y_{n},$ the statistic $S_{xy}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}{y}_{i}-\frac{1}{n}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & =2\,964-\frac{1}{30}(315)(278) \\  & =2\,964-2\,919 \\  & =45.\end{aligned}
$$
